html:
The Hodegetria was the most honoured icon of Constantinople: a painting of the Virgin Mary pointing to the Christ child in her arms, which Byzantines believed Saint Luke had painted from life. It was destroyed when the city fell in 1453.

The name means "she who shows the way". The icon was kept at the Hodegon monastery, and every week it was carried through the streets. In sieges it was taken along the walls, and Byzantines credited it with saving the city from Avars, Arabs and Rus. Its type, Mary holding the child and pointing to him, became one of the most copied images in Orthodox and Catholic art.

During the siege of 1453 it was moved to the Chora church near the land walls. When the Ottomans broke in, soldiers found it there. The historian Doukas wrote that they hacked it into pieces and shared out its gilded frame. Its end stood for the end of Byzantium itself.
sum: The Hodegetria was the most honoured icon of Constantinople: a painting of the Virgin Mary pointing to the Christ child in her arms, which Byzantines believed Saint Luke had painted from life. It was destroyed when the city fell in 1453.
